To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
polyamine analogues can be used to control the levels of hypusine and that the hypusine content of cells is a function of the polyamine composition of the cell.
the hypusine level in JURK AT cells is diminished by polyamine analogues that are effective in lowering putrescine, spermidine, and spermine levels.
the polyamine analogues DENSPM and (4,5)-triamine are potent at lowering the hypusine content of human JURKAT lymphoblasts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the polyamine hypusine in the growth and differentiation of T-cells.

the effects of polyamine analogs, which are known to be inhibitors of eukaryotic protein synthesis, on hypusine and its biosynthetic precursors, deoxyhypusinate, deoxyhypu sine, and deoxyhypu sine synthase.
the development of methods to measure hypusine in tissues, as well as with the effects of polyamine analogs on the biosynthesis and levels of hypusine in a human T- cell line.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hypusine content of JURKAT cell extracts is reduced by the analogues in the following order: DENSPM > or = DEHSPM >> (4,5 triamine) > or = (5,5 triamine).
the polyamine analogues are not effective inhibitors of hypusine biosynthesis in JURKAt T-cells.
polyamine analogues are effective in lowering intracellular hypuine levels in a T-cell line.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the polyamine analogues are active at controlling polyamine levels in JURKAt cells, but only DENSPM and, to a lesser extent, DEHSPM, are effective in lowering hypusine levels.
DENSPM is the most potent analogue for controlling cell growth and lowering hypusine levels, while DEHSPM is more effective in diminishing the hypusine content of cells.
DENSPM and, to a lesser extent, DEHSPM have the ability to lower spermidine, hypusine, and spermine levels in a human lymphoblastoid T-cell line.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the analogues do not have a direct effect on the biosynthesis of deoxyhypusinate or hypusine, but that they act by lowering the levels of putrescine, spermidine, and spermine, which, in turn, diminish the availability of these polyamines for the biosynthesis of the aminopropyl moiety of deoxyhypu sine.
the polyamine analogues are effective at reducing hypusine levels, and the extent of the reduction is related to the effectiveness of the analogue at reducing spermidine levels.
hypusine is sensitive to the polyamine analogues and can serve as a biomarker for polyamine depletion in cells.
